Carmen: quick heads-up — saw a perf regression on the continuous-batcher after the multi-variant routing change this morning. batch_fill_rate dropped a lot when compat sets got larger. :eyes:
Ilana: ugh. any KV cache numbers? seems like mix of fragmentation + kvcache churn usually.
Carmen: kvcache looks noisy. short dump below — noticed a lot more misses for the small-variant requests that fallback to the larger model.
Carmen: ```
kvcache stats (15m window):
  hits: 3.2k
  misses: 9.8k
  hit_rate: 24.5%
  avg_entry_size: 1.8kb
```
Samir: that hit_rate is brutal. does the batcher show more tiny batches or just slower kernel selection?
Carmen: both: avg batch size for pool A went 6.8 -> 3.1; scheduler spend up, kernel_select time up. quick profile snapshot:```
PROFILE: 60s sample
  batcher.waiting_form: 42.1%
  kernel_select: 18.3%
  scheduler.overhead: 27.1%
  kv_cache_ops: 12.5% (miss heavy)
```
Nori: so multi-variant routing expanded compatset membership and we get interleaved sequences that don't share KV prefixes -> less reuse, more small batches.
Ilana: right. fallback behavior amplifies it: when a request arrives and the preferred variant is cold, we send to fallback variant; that forces incompat sets in the batcher.
Samir: short-term mitigations? 1) raise token_budget for short seqs so they can coalesce? 2) add a small holdback window to let compatible requests arrive? 3) prefer sticky routing for sessions where we see repeated prefixes.
Carmen: tried a quick dogfood: +25% token_budget for pool A + 10ms slotting jitter -> batch_fill_rate 0.55 -> 0.78, p50 latency down ~9%. not perfect but promising.
Ilana: nice. can we avoid global token_budget change? maybe only for requests routed to multi-variant pools.
Nori: also think we should tighten compatset hashing to prefer variant families (e.g., quantized variants grouped) so batcher sees them as compatible when kernel selection is equivalent.
Samir: beware kernel selection semantics: we must only group if kernels and kv layout are compatible. maybe add a compat-tag that is computed at routing time and plumbs through the batcher.
Carmen: agreed. I'll prototype a "compat-tag" in the forwarder that maps fallback chains -> tag. then batcher uses tag + model id.
Ilana: can you capture a short repro script? QA wants to run with canary.
Carmen: repro gist (short):```bash
# spawn mixed-variant traffic: 70% small-quant, 30% large-fallback
wrk -t8 -c200 --script mixed_variant.lua http://canary.internal/generate
```
Carmen: deploy-bot pushed a quick canary with token_budget bump and compat-tagging flip on flag "feature/mv-compat-tag". :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary deployed to pool A @2425001400 (flag: mv-compat-tag=true, token_budget=1.25x)
Nori: can you collect kvcache and batcher histograms for the next hour? let's compare before/after.
Samir: I'll add a sampling profiler to capture kernel selection histogram and batch sizes; will post results.
Ilana: if this is positive we should:
  - short-term: enable compat-tag for multi-variant pools only
  - medium: add per-pool token_budget tuning UI in console
  - long-term: consider routing-level affinity and variant family clustering
Carmen: action items: Carmen -> prototype compat-tag + repro (EOD), Samir -> profiler job (2h), Ilana -> telemetry dashboard for batch_fill_rate + kvcache_hit_rate (tomorrow), Nori -> verify kernel compatibility rules for tagging.
Samir: noted. I'll start profiler now.
Carmen: thanks all. will post numbers in this thread once canary runs for 20m. :thumbsup:
